requests.need: Finite linear groups in characteristic p ∈ {2, 3}: (1) Dickson's classification of the finite subgroups of PGL_2(F̄_p) (cyclic, dihedral, A_4, S_4, A_5, PSL_2(𝔽_q), PGL_2(𝔽_q), subgroups of a Borel), and of SL_2(F̄_2) ≅ PGL_2(F̄_2); (2) a nontrivial p-subgroup of GL_2(F̄_p) fixes a unique line, its normaliser lies in the stabilising Borel, and its elements are unipotent; (3) a finite abelian subgroup of GL_2(F̄) has a common eigenvector. RS-06 assigns the generic finite GL_2/PGL_2 image classification to R01.4. DP23 Lemma 1.13: for odd p and odd ρ̄, absolute irreducibility over ℚ(√p*) is equivalent to absolute irreducibility over ℚ(ζ_p), with the dihedral conclusion when it fails.

Coefficient-field descent for residual representations: a continuous ρ̄ : G_ℚ → GL_2(F̄_p) (discrete topology) has finite image and takes values in GL_2(F) for a finite subfield F; absolute irreducibility is defined over F̄ and invariant under extension of scalars along F ⊆ F′. RS-06 assigns the finite coefficient-field carrier to R01.1.

The local carriers of a continuous ρ̄ : G_ℚ → GL_2(F): decomposition and inertia subgroups at a prime ℓ, the predicate 'unramified at ℓ' (ρ̄(I_ℓ) = 1), wild inertia at p, oddness det ρ̄(c) = −1 for complex conjugation, and the identification of ρ̄ restricted to a decomposition group at p with an injective homomorphism Gal(K_𝔭/ℚ_p) → GL_2(F) for the kernel field K, carrying inertia and wild inertia to their images.

For a finite extension E/ℚ_p: the different exponent d(E/ℚ_p), the ramification index, discriminantExponent = f·d, the exact tame exponent d = e − 1, and for E/ℚ_p Galois the upper ramification filtration with Herbrand functions (the identity for unramified extensions and x ↦ x/2 on [0, ∞) for a tame quadratic one), and the discriminant exponent in upper numbering, c = Σ_{i ≥ −1} ([G : G^{i+}] − [G : G^i])(i + 1) (Jones (1)). Upstream Layer 3 plans the different, the Hilbert valuation formula and the upper numbering; the displayed formula is the form consumed here.
The tame quotient: I/P is procyclic and a Frobenius lift σ acts on it by τ ↦ τ^q (upstream Layer 4, 'σ τ σ⁻¹ = τ^q'), in the finite form for Gal(E/ℚ_p).

The unit filtration U(K, i) of a nonarchimedean local field, on which R25.1/unit-filtration-power-maps proves the p-th power inclusions of Fesenko–Vostokov I.(5.7)–(5.8) in the three small cases used here.

Local class field theory for a finite abelian extension L/K of p-adic fields: the reciprocity map K^× → Gal(L/K), onto from units when L/K is totally ramified, carrying U^{(n)} onto the upper ramification group Gal(L/K)^{(n)} (Fesenko–Vostokov IV.(3.5)), and equivariant for automorphisms: rec(σ(u)) = σ̃ rec(u) σ̃^{−1} when L/K′ is Galois with K/K′ Galois and σ̃ lifts σ ∈ Gal(K/K′). Over ℚ_2 this gives: the inertia group of a finite abelian extension of exponent 2 is a quotient of ℤ_2^×/(ℤ_2^×)². The conductor exponents of quadratic characters of a local field K of absolute ramification e over ℚ_2: 0, the even integers at most 2e, and 2e + 1 (used with e = 2 for the case l = 13).

For a finite Galois number field K and a prime 𝔓 of 𝓞_K above p: the exponent of 𝔓 in the different ideal equals the local different exponent d(K_𝔓/ℚ_p), and (with Layer 5) Gal(K_𝔓/ℚ_p) is identified with the decomposition group of 𝔓, compatibly with inertia and ramification groups.

The explicit formula for the discriminant (Odlyzko 1990, (2.3)): for a number field K and an even differentiable F : ℝ → ℝ with F(0) = 1 and |F(x)|, |F′(x)| ≤ c e^{−(1/2+ε)|x|}, log |d_K| = r₁π/2 + n(γ + log 8π) − n∫_0^∞ (1 − F)/(2 sinh(x/2)) − r₁∫_0^∞ (1 − F)/(2 cosh(x/2)) − 4∫_0^∞ F(x) cosh(x/2) dx + Σ′_ρ Φ(ρ) + 2Σ_𝔓 Σ_{m≥1} (log N𝔓/N𝔓^{m/2}) F(m log N𝔓), with Φ(s) = ∫ F(x) e^{(s−1/2)x} dx and ρ over the nontrivial zeros of ζ_K. It rests on the completed Dedekind zeta function of AnalyticNumberTheory AN.4 (continuation, functional equation, Hadamard product). AN.3 plans the explicit formulas.

Fontaine's ramification bound (Il n'y a pas de variété abélienne sur Z, Théorème A) for a finite flat group scheme killed by p over a complete DVR of absolute ramification e, exported in the normalisation of R25.1: the field L generated by its points satisfies δ(L_λ) < e(1 + 1/(p − 1)) at primes above p. R07.6 already plans this bound and the convention translation.

Over ℤ and ℤ[1/N]: (a) the scheme-theoretic closure of a Galois-stable subgroup of G(ℚ̄) is a closed flat subgroup scheme, so a simple finite flat group scheme is killed by a prime and its generic Galois module is simple; (b) the Oort–Tate classification of group schemes of prime order p over ℤ[1/N]; (c) the gluing equivalence between finite flat group schemes over ℤ[1/N] and triples over ℤ[1/pN], ℤ_p and ℚ_p, with the resulting exact Hom–Ext¹ sequence (Schoof, Math. Ann. 325 (2003), Proposition 2.4); (d) the connected–étale splitting over ℤ_p of an extension of μ_p by ℤ/pℤ; (e) étale group schemes over ℤ[1/N] as Galois modules of π₁(Spec ℤ[1/N]). R07.1 plans Cartier duality, connected–étale sequences, generic subgroup closures and fpqc descent. (f) The Katz–Mazur group schemes G_ε over ℤ[1/l] for units ε (Katz–Mazur, Interlude 8.7): extensions of ℤ/pℤ by μ_p whose points generate ℚ(ζ_p, ε^{1/p}); and the twisted constant schemes V(ρ) attached to representations unramified outside l∞. (g) The same gluing sequence over ℤ[1/l].

For an abelian scheme 𝒜 of relative dimension g over ℤ: 𝒜[n] finite flat of order n^{2g}; the quotient of 𝒜 by a finite flat subgroup scheme is an abelian scheme; the Weil pairing identifies the Cartier dual of 𝒜[n] with 𝒜^∨[n]; degrees of isogenies are multiplicative and a separable isogeny has kernel of order its degree. The same torsion, quotient and Weil-pairing statements over ℤ[1/l]. Tate modules of GL₂-type abelian varieties over ℚ.
The dual abelian variety and a polarization, which is an isogeny A → A^∨, over a finite field. The polarization isogeny over the residue fields of ℤ[1/l, ζ_l].

For an abelian variety A over 𝔽_q: the q-power Frobenius endomorphism F, the separability of 1 − F (its differential is the identity), and #A(𝔽_q) = deg(1 − F). End⁰ of an abelian variety over ℚ and the freeness of V_p(A) over K ⊗ ℚ_p for GL₂(K)-type A.

An abelian variety over ℚ with good reduction at every prime extends to an abelian scheme over ℤ (its Néron model), and conversely. R11.1 plans 'Compare good reduction with an abelian-scheme model'. Good reduction at every prime other than l gives an abelian scheme over ℤ[1/l].

The monodromy criterion in the form used by Schoof: for an abelian variety over ℚ with semistable reduction at l, every σ in an inertia group above l satisfies (σ − 1)² = 0 on the p-adic Tate module for p ≠ l (Grothendieck, SGA 7 IX 3.5). RS-06 links R11.3 to R25.4. The same criterion is used for the realising abelian varieties of R25.5.

Global class field theory in the explicit form used for Schoof's cases: for a number field M and a modulus 𝔪, abelian extensions of M of conductor dividing 𝔪 correspond to quotients of the ray class group Cl_𝔪(M), an extension of Cl(M) by (𝓞_M/𝔪)^× modulo the image of the global units; over ℚ this is Kronecker–Weber for conductors lᵏ∞. The conductor–discriminant formula for a relative abelian extension is used with it. An abelian extension of a number field unramified at every place has degree dividing the class number; and for p ≡ 3 (mod 4) the class number of ℚ(√−p) is odd (genus theory).

Potential modularity of a given weight-two lift in Snowden's form (his Theorem 5.1.2): for ρ : G_ℚ → GL₂(ℚ̄_p) finitely ramified, odd, of weight two with (A1), a finite totally real Galois F″/ℚ linearly disjoint from any given finite extension, and a parallel weight two Hilbert eigenform over F″ realising ρ|G_{F″}.
Solvable descent: along a Galois extension with 2-group Galois group, a parallel weight two Hilbert eigenform realising ρ upstairs descends to one realising ρ on the fixed field.
Jacquet–Langlands to a quaternion algebra over a totally real field of odd degree split at exactly one infinite place, preserving Hecke eigenvalues.

For a parallel weight two eigenform transferred to such a quaternion algebra, its Galois representation occurs in the Tate module of the Jacobian of the Shimura curve (Hida, Theorem 4.12), giving a GL₂-type abelian variety (Snowden Lemma 9.4.3).
Faltings's isogeny theorem over number fields, End ⊗ ℚ_p = End_{G_F}(V_p), used for restrictions of scalars in Snowden's descent lemma.

Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich and Grothendieck's criteria in λ-adic form for GL₂-type abelian varieties, the independence of λ of their Weil–Deligne representations (including λ above the residue characteristic, through the p-adic comparison of R06), and good/semistable reduction at p from crystalline/semistable V_λ.

At (p, k) ∈ {(3, 2), (3, 4), (5, 6), (7, 8), (13, 14)}: the crystalline-to-ordinary criterion (Fontaine–Laffaille for k ≤ p, Berger–Li–Zhu for k = p + 1) for crystalline representations with Hodge–Tate weights {0, k − 1} and reducible reduction, and Skinner–Wiles modularity for the resulting ordinary p-distinguished representations with residual 1 ⊕ ω^{k−1}; also the Serre weight (ℓ + 1 or 2 up to twist) of the reduction of a crystalline representation with Hodge–Tate weights {0, ℓ} or {0, 1}.

The lifts of DP23 Theorem 1.9(3)–(4) and KW04 Theorem 3.1: a minimal crystalline lift of Hodge–Tate weights {0, k(ρ̄) − 1}, and for k(ρ̄) = p + 1 a weight-two lift of Steinberg type at p, unramified outside p for level-one ρ̄.
The compatible system through such a lift, with good reduction everywhere (crystalline at the places of odd residue characteristic) in the level-one crystalline case (KW04 Theorem 3.1(i)).

Serre's weight recipe in the forms used: the normalisation 2 ≤ k ≤ p + 1 by twisting, parity (k even at level one), the θ-shift k(ρ̄ ⊗ ω) = k + p + 1 for 2 ≤ k ≤ p − 1, and the weights of niveau-one dihedral representations.

sourceIssues.reason: Herbrand's theorem concerns the eigenspaces ω^{1−k} with k even and p ∤ B_k; the ω²-eigenspace is reached from the ω^{−1}-eigenspace by reflection. Schoof's errata note states exactly this. Nothing in this checkpoint depends on it: over ℤ with p = 2 the character group is trivial and the class group of ℤ[1/2] is trivial; the p = 3 cases of R25.4 must use the corrected step.

sourceIssues.locator: §6, proof of Theorem 1.1, Case l = 7, p = 3, p. 858 (also arXiv:math/0502356)
sourceIssues.printed: The source uses Odlyzko's bounds to claim that every unramified extension of K′ has relative degree strictly below 120/36 < 4.
sourceIssues.correction: K′ is cubic over K = Q(ζ3, ζ7 + ζ7^{−1}, 7^{1/3}), which has degree 18, so [K′ : Q] = 54 and the relative degree is smaller than 120/54 < 3.
sourceIssues.reason: The root discriminant 3^{25/18}7^{2/3} ≈ 16.83 bounds the absolute degree of an unramified extension of K′ by 119 (Odlyzko's Table 2 gives 17.020 at n = 120); dividing by [K′ : Q] = 54, not 36, gives the relative bound. The argument only needs to exclude degrees 2 and 3, so the weaker printed bound still suffices.

sourceIssues.printed: The source writes cond(χ) = (1 + i)^a with a ⩽ 2, then deduces a ⩽ 3 from v2(δL) < 2.
sourceIssues.correction: for some a ⩾ 0; the bound a ⩽ 3 then comes from v₂(δ_L) < 2, and wild ramification with the absence of conductor exponent 3 gives a = 2.
sourceIssues.reason: If a ⩽ 2 were known, the next sentence (a ⩽ 3) would be redundant; the parallel step in Case l = 5 (Step 1) writes 'for some a ⩾ 0'. The bound comes from v₂(δ_L) = 1 + a/4 < 2.
